results.name: Girl with a Pearl Earring – 3D Bust Model
results.description:
A 3D digital sculpture reimagining Johannes Vermeer’s masterwork Girl with a Pearl Earring in full three-dimensional form, mounted on a round pedestal base. 
* Subject: Three-quarter view portrait bust capturing her famous over-the-shoulder gaze, parted lips, and large pearlescent earring. 
* Texture & Detail: Features soft skin tones and dynamic lighting highlights on the metallic earring reflection, lips, and eyes. 
* Attire: Vibrant blue turban with an elongated yellow fabric drop, set over an ochre/mustard jacket with a white collar band and light blue trim. 
* Base & Presentation: Sculpted onto a circular display pedestal for a classic gallery-style bust layout. 
* Use Cases: Suitable for digital art galleries, virtual museum exhibitions, educational EdTech modules, AR/VR spatial applications, and 3D web viewers.

results.name: Jaguar-Head Urn
results.description:
Polychrome urn (black, orange, and white) with slightly curved, divergent walls and a pedestal base. It is decorated with a jaguar head in relief, featuring an open mouth displaying teeth and foreclaws. The figure wears disk-shaped ear ornaments and a collar defined by a pinched circumferential band, along with three disk-shaped medallions on the pedestal. Three vertical bands decorated with spike motifs, resembling the trunk of a young ceiba tree, complete the remainder of the surface. From the Ixil Region.
 IDAEH Cultural Property No. 11.2.179.0198
www.fundacionrutamaya.org

Special thanks to the staff of La Ruta Maya Foundation for their hard work on this project.

3D model made using Artec Leo

results.name: Colonoware Pedestalled Base Sherd with Etchings
results.description:
In much of West and Central Africa, earthenware pots are used for medicinal and spiritual practices. On South Carolina plantations, some captive workers used the pottery as containers for preparing herbal medicines and making charms. Archaeologists found colonoware pots marked with an incised “X,” or other marks, signifying their spiritual importance. The X is associated with a ritualistic symbol known as the cosmogram. The cosmogram typically takes the form of a cross and represents the cycle of life, death, and rebirth, with a watery barrier separating the world of the living from the spirit world of those who have died.

This base of a pedestaled bowl was found at Mepkin Plantation on the Cooper River in Berkeley County. The mark etched into the exterior resembles a cosmogram, and the mark on the interior may represent vanga, or the highest knowledge that specialists and leaders strive to achieve.

This artifact is currently on display at the [Gullah Museum](https://tinyurl.com/4dd9trzy) in Georgetown, SC.
